hello.note: For anyone, at any time. God dag (goo DAAG) is formal

how-are-you.note: The h in hv is silent. Norwegians say du, you, to everyone

goodbye.note: Literally "have it good". Often just Ha det

please.note: Literally "be so kind", used for real favours. In shops, Norwegians put takk at the end instead: En kaffe, takk

thank-you.note: Tusen takk (TÜ-sen tak), a thousand thanks, means thank you very much

no.note: Nei takk is no, thank you

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention or get past

my-name.note: The audio uses Peter as the example name

speak-english.note: Nearly every Norwegian speaks excellent English

thousand.note: Prices are in kroner (KROO-ner), written kr or NOK

would-like.note: The polite way to order. The audio uses en kaffe (ehn KAF-feh), a coffee
would-like.spoken: Jeg vil gjerne ha en kaffe

i-want.note: Literally "I'll take...". The audio uses denne (DEN-neh), this one

do-you-have.note: Dere is "you all", the usual way to ask a shop. The audio uses vann (van), water

too-expensive.note: Norway is among the most expensive countries in the world

card.note: Cards and phones are taken almost everywhere

bill.note: Service is included; rounding up is a nice extra

taxi.text: Kan du ringe etter en taxi?
taxi.say: kan dü RING-eh ET-ter ehn TAK-see
taxi.note: Taxis are very expensive; trains, buses and ferries are excellent

train.note: The Oslo to Bergen line is one of the world's great train rides

train-station.note: The main station in a city is often Sentralstasjon

which-train.note: The audio uses Bergen (BAIR-gen) as the example

buy-ticket.note: Tickets are mostly bought in the Vy app

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Bergen as the example

trip-length.text: Hvor lang tid tar det til...?
trip-length.say: vor lang teed taar deh til ...
trip-length.note: The audio uses Bergen as the example
trip-length.spoken: Hvor lang tid tar det til Bergen?
trip-length.filled: Hvor lang tid tar det til ⟦Bergen⟧?

delicious.note: Literally "lovely", said of food and much else

allergic.note: Add the food: nøtter (NÖT-ter) nuts, peanøtter (PEH-a-nöt-ter) peanuts, skalldyr (SKAL-dür) shellfish. The audio uses nuts

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

beer.note: Beer is expensive. Shops sell only light beer; stronger drinks come from the state shop, Vinmonopolet

water.note: Tap water is excellent and free

cheers.note: Look each person in the eye
